clue.text: Smart, deleting line in permit? The opposite

indicators.note: in tells us the trimmed word goes inside the word for permit

parts.note: a visa is a permit to enter a country

indicators.note: deleting tells us to drop the letter standing for line

parts.note: smart means clever

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a smart document has had a line struck out of a permit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deleting' takes L from CLEVER to leave CEVER, which goes 'in' VISA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means the reverse holds true, which is exactly what 'the opposite' asserts.

clue.text: Start to comment on hat worn once by British subject

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: a topi is a sun helmet worn by the British in colonial India

indicators.note: Start to means take only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A remark about a sun helmet once favoured by a British colonial subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British subject' looks like one phrase, but 'British' belongs to the hat and 'subject' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject of discussion is a theme or matter talked about.

clue.text: Proper tease, one that's under your skin

parts.note: proper as in genuine, real
to rib someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: Teasing someone properly is something that gets under their skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under your skin' suggests annoyance, but it is literal: a rib lies beneath the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A true rib is one attached to the breastbone, a bone lying beneath the skin of the chest.

clue.text: Journeyman fell on part of face, twisting

indicators.note: in an across clue, the word for fell placed on the face part comes after it
twisting tells us to turn the part of the face round so it reads backwards

parts.note: the lip is part of the face
fell as an adjective means fierce or grim

explanation.surface: A travelling worker tumbles onto his face and twists it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like a verb (fell over) but is the old adjective meaning cruel; 'on' puts it after PIL, the lip turned round by 'twisting'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrim is someone making a journey, here wittily cast as a journey-man.

clue.text: Find a source of filthy lucre?

definitions.text: Find a source of filthy lucre?

parts.words: Find a source of filthy lucre?
parts.note: filthy lucre is money; read literally, finding money in soil is striking earth that pays off

explanation.surface: Someone discovers where dirty money comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to strike it rich, finding a profitable seam, as miners hit valuable ground.

clue.text: Bird's vital little sound

indicators.note: sound tells us the answer is how the words are said aloud

parts.note: vital means key and little means wee, giving key wee

explanation.surface: A bird's tiny call is essential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird's' is 'Bird is', the definition, with the rest said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: The kiwi is a flightless bird of New Zealand.

clue.text: Wild golfer almost hides

indicators.note: hides tells us the answer is concealed inside the run of words golfer almost

explanation.surface: A furious golfer nearly hides away.
explanation.definitionFit: Feral describes animals living in a wild state after being domesticated.

clue.text: Nameless bird at height in faint illumination

indicators.note: Nameless means remove the letter standing for name

parts.note: the starling is a common bird

explanation.surface: An anonymous bird flies high in dim light.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the abbreviation for name, removed from STARLING to leave STARLIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Light from the stars is a faint glow in the night sky.

clue.text: Next to storage area in large quantities

definitions.meaning: beside a yard, the enclosure where goods are kept
sold in bulk, measured out by length

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means beside a yard and idiomatically means in great amounts.

clue.text: Ineffective large bird?

parts.note: ineffective means of no use, with O for nothing: zero use
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A big bird that is useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ineffective large bird' reads as one useless creature; 'large' is just L.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel is an old name for the blackbird, also used of the ring ouzel.

clue.text: Announced I have bought a piece of Scotland

indicators.note: Announced tells us to say the words aloud and hear the answer

parts.note: if I have bought something I own it; the indefinite article, A

explanation.surface: Someone declares they have purchased a bit of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a small island of the Inner Hebrides, off Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: Simply dare to be different — I mean it

indicators.note: to be different tells us the letters are rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: A challenge to be bold and stand out, said with conviction.
explanation.definitionFit: The catchphrase is an emphatic way of saying a promise is serious.

clue.text: Walk between trees: such a lawyer would limp?

parts.note: someone who would limp is lame
a DA is a district attorney, an American lawyer

explanation.surface: A lawyer with a limp strolls down an avenue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such' links: the lawyer is a lame DA.
explanation.definitionFit: An alameda is a Spanish-style promenade lined with trees.

clue.text: Female soldier is less evasive

parts.note: a ranker is a soldier in the ranks

explanation.surface: A woman soldier is more direct.
explanation.definitionFit: Franker means more open and candid, so less evasive.

clue.text: Office-holder's advice once to include Liberal rejected

indicators.note: rejected tells us the built word is turned back to front
to include means the word for advice takes the letter for Liberal inside it

parts.note: rede is an archaic word for advice

explanation.surface: An official's old counsel to bring in a Liberal was turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' puts L inside REDE to give REDLE, which 'rejected' turns back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder holds office in a church, such as a Presbyterian elder.

clue.text: Retain young professional showing football skill

parts.note: to retain is to keep
a yuppy is a young urban professional

explanation.surface: A club holds onto a young professional with fancy footwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping a football in the air with repeated touches is a playground skill.

clue.text: Double-check the fodder

parts.note: to vet is to check thoroughly
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: Inspect the animal feed twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double' means two words for check, side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Vetch is a leguminous plant grown as animal fodder.

clue.text: Not allowed to be under this return attack

definitions.text: Not allowed to be under this
definitions.meaning: goods sold under the ... are sold illicitly
a ...-attack is a blow struck back

explanation.definitionFit: A shop counter conceals illicit sales, and a counter is a retaliatory blow.

clue.text: At last, spectator sees Villa thrashing Palace

indicators.note: thrashing tells us the letters are beaten into a new order
At last means take only the final letter of spectator

explanation.surface: A fan finally watches Aston Villa beat Crystal Palace.
explanation.walkthrough: Villa (Aston Villa) and Palace (Crystal Palace) are English football clubs, which hides the French royal palace.
explanation.definitionFit: Versailles is the grand royal palace built by Louis XIV near Paris.

clue.text: Infectious sailor free to go round

indicators.note: to go round means the word for free encircles the sailor

parts.note: to rid is to free
AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: A contagious seaman is released to roam.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabies is infectious, so rabid describes a carrier of that disease.

clue.text: Unopened picnic basket on beach, a symbol of togetherness

indicators.note: Unopened means the basket loses its first letter

parts.note: a hamper is a picnic basket
sand covers a beach

explanation.surface: An unopened picnic hamper on the beach as a token of companionship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unopened' takes the opening H off the basket; 'a symbol of togetherness' sounds abstract but is the sign meaning 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampersand is the sign for 'and', the word that joins things together.

clue.text: Money-box son leaves undisturbed

indicators.note: leaves tells us the letter for son departs from the word

parts.note: undisturbed means still

explanation.surface: A son leaves the cash box untouched.
explanation.definitionFit: A till is a drawer or box holding a shop's cash.

clue.text: Leaving something in one's hair

definitions.meaning: the line where hair is combed in two directions

explanation.definitionFit: A parting is both a farewell and the dividing line in combed hair.

clue.text: Mother holds hand during lowest point, getting ordered to prison

indicators.note: during means the mother-and-hand piece sits within the low point

parts.note: a col is the lowest point of a ridge between two peaks

indicators.note: holds means the word for mother contains the hand

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: Mother clings to someone's hand at a low moment as they are sent down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' and 'during' each nest one piece inside another; a col is a mountain pass, the dip between two peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Committal is the formal sending of someone to prison or for trial.

clue.text: Cocktail old boy's drunk with girl

indicators.note: drunk tells us the letters are reeling into a new order

parts.note: the words old boy, with the possessive adding no letter
Mary is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An old man, drunk, with his girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bloody Mary is a cocktail of vodka and tomato juice.

clue.text: Make up cabaret, if, alternatively, a brief act is out of order

indicators.note: is out of order tells us the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Invent a cabaret, or failing that a short act gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cabaret, if, alternatively' is a second anagram of the same letters, giving the solver two routes to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To fabricate a story is to make it up, invent it.

clue.text: Fish flop at last on vessel where youngsters may be on board

definitions.text: where youngsters may be on board

parts.note: the skate is a flat fish

indicators.note: at last means take only the final letter of flop

parts.note: an ark is a vessel, as Noah's

explanation.surface: A fish flops at the end of its life aboard a boat full of children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a ship, but means on a skateboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A skatepark is a facility with ramps for skateboarders.

clue.text: Army drank in mess, out of this?

definitions.text: Army drank in mess, out of this?

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

indicators.note: in mess means the letters are jumbled, with a nod to the officers' mess

explanation.surface: Soldiers drank in their mess hall, from these vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: what soldiers drink from.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankard is a large drinking mug, typically for beer.

clue.text: Be so supportive for friend in robbery

definitions.meaning: to ... for a friend is to defend them

explanation.definitionFit: A stick-up is an armed robbery, and to stick up for someone is to defend them.

clue.text: Remove all this writer's enemies?

parts.note: read as a command, de- means remove and foe means enemy, so this author's name sounds like de-enemy

explanation.surface: A request to rid an author of all his foes.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe was the English writer of Robinson Crusoe.

clue.text: Sneering, in the manner of a small island?

parts.note: Sark is a small Channel Island
the suffix -y makes an adjective meaning like or in the manner of

explanation.surface: Being sarcastic in the style of a small island.
explanation.walkthrough: SARKY is British slang for sarcastic.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarky is informal British for sarcastic, which is sneering in tone.

clue.text: Drop and split

definitions.meaning: a drop of water from the eye

explanation.definitionFit: A tear is a drop from the eye, and a tear is a rip or split.
